# ↩️ Rollback Checklist

## Incident metadata

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Incident/change ID | |
| Affected environment | |
| Current revision | |
| Target rollback revision | |
| Decision owner | |
| Operator | |
| Start time | |

## Trigger and impact

Describe the observable failure, affected user tasks, impact scope, and why rollback is safer than a forward fix.

## Safety checks

- [ ] Rollback revision is known and verified
- [ ] Artifact/configuration compatibility is understood
- [ ] Data migrations and irreversible changes are assessed
- [ ] Current logs and evidence are preserved safely
- [ ] Stakeholders are informed
- [ ] Rollback owner and escalation path are available

## Execution record

| Step | Action | Expected result | Actual result | Timestamp |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | | | | |
| 2 | | | | |
| 3 | | | | |

## Verification

Verify expected routes, primary interactions, service health, and any data consistency requirements. If persistence is introduced in future, follow a separately tested recovery plan.

## Follow-up

- Root cause:
- Corrective action:
- Regression test:
- Owner:
- Target date:
- Post-incident review:
